source.title_on_document: ChatGPT decreases idea diversity in brainstorming

paper_design_summary: A Matters Arising reanalysis of the public data from Lee and Chung (2024), whose experiments randomized participants to generate one idea each with ChatGPT, with web search, or unaided. The authors pool each condition's ideas and compute the fraction of unique idea concepts, where two ideas overlap when the cosine similarity of their Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings exceeds 0.8. They compare this set-level diversity across conditions in six experiment panels (1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4, 5); Experiment 2b also includes ideas generated by ChatGPT alone.

outcomes.name: Fraction of unique ideas in the condition's idea pool (threshold 0.8)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Share of unique, non-overlapping idea concepts in each condition's pool: number of unique concepts divided by total ideas; two ideas overlap when pairwise cosine similarity of Google Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings exceeds 0.8 (main analysis). Robustness variants in Supplementary Information (not in this PDF): thresholds 0.75 and 0.85; aggregated comparisons of similarity scores; pairwise comparisons of similarity scores; mean edge distance in minimum spanning trees. Could also be read as category_count (count of unique ideas by thresholded clustering).

contrasts.reported: Unique fraction: Web-search-assisted 0.96 vs ChatGPT-assisted 0.74 (bar labels; error bars = 95% CIs for individual proportions, not printed as numbers). Text: AI-aided sets less diverse in all five experiments, significant in four of five, the non-significant one being experiment 4. Tests and Bonferroni-corrected CIs for differences are in Supplementary Table 1 (not in this PDF).
contrasts.locator: p. 1108 (PDF p. 2), Fig. 1 panel 'Experiment 1' and text

diversity_detail.metric: Fraction of unique idea concepts (unique concepts / total ideas), overlap defined as USE cosine similarity > 0.8
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of ideas within each condition's pool; one value per condition (set level)
diversity_detail.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals for individual proportions shown as error bars in Fig. 1; Bonferroni-corrected confidence intervals for differences in Supplementary Table 1 (not in this PDF); test type not stated in the main text
diversity_detail.notes: Higher = more diverse; no sign reversal needed.

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Lee, B. C. & Chung, J. J. (2024). An empirical investigation of the impact of ChatGPT on creativity. Nature Human Behaviour 8, 1906-1914 (doi 10.1038/s41562-024-01953-1). This paper is a secondary analysis of all of Lee and Chung's experiments (public OSF data, https://osf.io/rzn87).
sample_overlap.quote: We answered these questions via additional analyses of the detailed and carefully reported publicly available data that Lee and Chung provide.
sample_overlap.locator: p. 1107 (PDF p. 1), right column; Reporting Summary, Study description: 'Secondary analysis of previously published data by Lee & Chung (2024)' (PDF p. 5)

company_involvement.description: Competing interests: 'The authors declare no competing interests.'

eligibility.reason: Reanalysis of Lee and Chung (2024), whose participants were randomized to ChatGPT, web search, or no aid (p. 1107). Criterion 2: the paper gives no total participant counts, but in Experiment 2A the ChatGPT arm alone has 96 ideas and each participant submitted one idea (p. 1107), so at least 96 people; counts for the other experiments are not in this document and should be taken from Lee and Chung (2024). Criterion 3: set-level diversity (fraction of unique ideas via embedding similarity) computed on participants' ideas. The sample is shared with Lee and Chung (2024); per codebook section 8 rule 4 this reanalysis can supply the across_people record that the original paper did not report. Design class coded 'other' because this document does not say whether the original experiments ran online, in a lab, or in the field. Experiment 2b's ChatGPT-only contrast is AI vs human output (context only).

one_line_finding: In a reanalysis of Lee and Chung's (2024) experiments, ChatGPT-aided idea pools had a lower fraction of unique ideas (embedding cosine threshold 0.8) than comparison pools in every experiment, e.g. 0.74 vs 0.96 (web search) in Experiment 1 and 0.70 vs 0.92 (human) and 0.91 (web search) in Experiment 2a, significant in four of five experiments (Fig. 1 and text, p. 1108).
open_questions: Fig. 1 shows six experiment panels (1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4, 5) but the text says 'all five experiments' and 'four out of five comparisons'; which five comparisons are counted (e.g., whether 2a and 2b are one experiment, or whether 2b's ChatGPT-only set is the comparison) is not stated in the main text.

Per-arm participant and idea counts, test statistics, and Bonferroni-corrected CIs for differences are in Supplementary Table 1, which is not in this PDF; counts should be taken from Lee and Chung (2024) or the SI.
Setting of the original experiments (online panel, lab, or field) and population are not stated in this document; design_class left as 'other' pending Lee and Chung (2024).
The 'ChatGPT-human' condition in Experiment 2b is not defined in this document.
How the second factor in Experiments 4 (high/low constraints) and 5 (base/high empathy) was assigned is not stated in this document.
notes: Matters Arising (3 pages) plus a 7-page Reporting Summary; PDF pages 4-10 are the Reporting Summary, which lists research sample, randomization, and data exclusions as N/A for this secondary analysis. Alternative diversity metrics (thresholds 0.75 and 0.85; aggregated and pairwise similarity comparisons; mean MST edge distance) are reported only in the Supplementary Information: '37 of the 45 comparisons yield statistically significant effects (Supplementary Table 1)' (p. 1108). Each participant submitted one idea, so set-level diversity is across different people. Lee and Chung's own individual-idea creativity ratings (with_ai) are described but not reanalyzed here. No per-study p-values or test statistics are printed in this PDF.
